key_insight: AnimalFarm examines how AI systems generate and detect hateful imagery featuring human-like, non-human characters. It introduces a systematic study of this underexplored safety risk, though the supplied abstract is incomplete and does not report results.
problem_solved: Hateful messages can target human groups indirectly through anthropomorphic characters, creating a safety challenge that has received limited systematic evaluation.
method: Construct a benchmark from conservatively screened source scenes.
Cover five types of anthropomorphic non-human characters.
Audit both hateful image generation and detection; further evaluation details are unavailable in the supplied abstract.
impact: This work highlights an overlooked area for image-generation safeguards and content moderation. Practitioners can use this research direction to broaden safety testing beyond imagery depicting humans directly.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram: screened source scenes → benchmark → generation and detection audits.
Five neutral character silhouettes representing the benchmark's character-type coverage.
A two-panel graphic contrasting image-generation safeguards with hateful-image detection.
An indirect-targeting diagram showing how fictional characters can convey hostility toward human groups, without reproducing hateful content.
paper_title: AnimalFarm: Auditing the Generation and Detection of Hateful Images Featuring Anthropomorphic Characters
paper_authors: Junjie Chu, Ye Leng, Mingjie Li, Yiting Qu, Michael Backes
